title: tempered-slo-reservoir-and-circuit-lull-respite
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Production has seen short-lived traffic spikes that flip regional circuits and trigger repeated failovers within a 60s window. These micro-flaps undermine tail-latency SLOs and generate noisy incident churn. This PR implements two complementary mitigations: 1) a lightweight per-region "SLO reservoir" that absorbs transient token bursts by allowing a small, time-bounded credit pool per SLO class and tenant cohort; 2) a "circuit lull respite" policy that imposes an adaptive reopen delay and a soft drain phase before full circuit restoration to reduce flip-flop. Motivation: previous mitigations (hard throttle/circuit immediate reopen) either impact steady traffic or allow rapid re-open/close cycles. The reservoir smooths short token bursts without degrading long-tail throughput; the lull respite stabilizes circuit state transitions. Design summary: reservoir: configurable credits expressed in token-ms (tokens*ms) per region and SLO tier, refill with exponential backoff when saturated, borrowing allowed across tenant cohorts within a reserve budget, overflow triggers a predictive soft-shed (prefers non-blocking degrade paths). circuit lull respite: state machine extension with LULL state between CLOSED and OPEN; LULL enforces slower reopen ramp (soft-concurrency limits + KV-preserve hints), records a lull_score derived from recent circuit events and telemetry, and extends reopen windows when score is high. Interaction and invariants: 1) reservoir deficits surface to the SLO controller which will prefer reservoir-backed admission over full circuit trip; 2) when reservoir exhausted, the existing circuit trip path remains intact; 3) lull respite consults reservoir pressure before permitting a transition to CLOSED to avoid reintroducing load. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, default off for all customers; staged canary to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48h, then 25% and 100% after metric stability checks. Telemetry and alerts: new metrics added: slo_reservoir_available_tokens, slo_reservoir_refill_rate, circuit_lull_score, circuit_lull_state_transitions. Alerting: reservoir_high_spill (>5% tenants spill for >5m) and lull_reopen_oscillation (>3 reopen-close cycles per minute). Testing: unit tests for credit math, property tests for refill/borrow semantics, e2e with synthetic burst harness in perf-lab, chaos test to validate circuit lull behavior under repeated spike patterns. Compatibility: conservative defaults maintain existing behavior; operators can tune reservoir sizes and lull thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-8421) [x] unit tests added [x] load tests in perf-lab executed [x] telemetry dashboards sketched [x] feature flag gating in place [x] docs/ops playbook updated Impact and rationale: reduces incident noise and preserves tail SLOs by smoothing transient demand and preventing immediate reopen churn. Related: this complements transient-hedge and graceful-evac modules (see ENG-8477). TODO/Follow-ups: automatic tuning loop (future work), RBAC controls for per-tenant overrides, and a UI control in Console for reservoir sizing.

review_comments: Aarav Singh: Nice approach. Please add guardrails to ensure a tiny reservoir can't be abused by high-concurrency bursty tenants.
Maya Chen: Added borrow cap and tenant-level max_credit in controller config; documented in ops playbook.
Priya Kapoor: Concern about metrics cardinality if we emit per-tenant tokens for every tenant. Can we aggregate?
Maya Chen: We only emit per-tenant spill events at 1m throttle and aggregate reservoir availability at region-tier level; added comment and ROI calc.
Liam O'Connor: Can we bump the default lull reopen ramp to be more conservative for Dedicated clusters?
Maya Chen: Exposed cluster_type override; default remains conservative for Dedicated in config
ci_checks: perf-regression: no change within noise (baseline run)
release_notes: Introduces a configurable SLO reservoir to smooth transient token bursts and a circuit lull respite policy to reduce reopen flip-flop. Defaults are opt-in behind a feature flag and safe for conservative rollouts. Adds telemetry and dashboards for monitoring reservoir pressure and circuit lull state.
notes: Operator action: enable feature flag for canary region and monitor slo_reservoir_available_tokens and circuit_lull_score. If spills observed, reduce reservoir size or enable soft-shed to avoid tenant impact.
